info.title: mxr HTTP Bridge
info.description: Local-first email daemon HTTP/WebSocket surface. This document is a route inventory plus the protocol schemas: it lists paths and methods, not per-route parameters or response bodies, and some live bridge routes are not declared here. All routes declared in this document except /api/v1/health require a bearer token, read from the `bridge-token` file in the active profile's config directory (`~/Library/Application Support/mxr` on macOS, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mxr` or `~/.config/mxr` on Linux). `[bridge].token_path` wins over `MXR_BRIDGE_TOKEN_PATH`, which wins over `MXR_CONFIG_DIR`.

AccountAddress.description:
One owned email address per account. Direction inference compares
`messages.from_email` against this set to decide inbound vs outbound.

health.description:
As of `generated_at`. A client ticking forward turns `ok` into
`stale` itself (`effective_health`).

label.description:
How the account is named in a warning: "Gmail" or "Outlook" when it
is the only account, else the account's own name, so two Gmail
accounts never read the same.

newest_message_at.description: The newest message received in any mailbox, whatever its mode.

oneOf.description: In-memory send provider for tests. Not for production use.
In-memory provider used for CLI smoke tests. Not for production use.

Live progress of the pass currently running, when one is. Held in
daemon memory rather than the status row: it changes far too often to
be worth a write per step, and it means nothing once the daemon that
reported it is gone.

dry_run.description:
True by default: a preview of the exact plan with its token. Only an
explicit `false`, with the preview's token and text, sends.

expect_text.description: The previewed text: the send refuses anything else.

preview_token.description: The preview's token, issued within the last minute.

AckPlanData.description:
Returned by `Request::AckMessage`: the exact acknowledgement Got it
sends, built from how you write to them (no model).

built_from.description:
"Your usual greeting and sign-off with Samir." or "No greeting or
sign-off of yours to go on, so a plain thanks."

countdown_seconds.description: Clients show the text this long before sending, with undo.

from.description: The address it is sent from.

html.description:
The exact HTML part that is sent, built from `text` by the same
builder: every value is escaped, so nothing in a name or greeting
becomes a link or markup.

preview_token.description:
Set on a preview: send with it, and `text`, within a minute. It binds
the recipient, sender, target message and text.

reply_to_message_id.description: The message being acknowledged: their latest.

oneOf.description: Set once sent.

text.description: The exact text that is sent, as its plain-text part.

to.description: Exactly one recipient: Got it never replies to all.

context.description: Parsed context; clients see structured JSON, not the raw string.

key.description:
Group key — depends on `group_by`: action token, ISO date, source,
target kind, or hour-of-day string `00`..`23`.

ActivityTier.description:
Mirror of `mxr_store::Tier`. Three retention buckets used by the
activity log: 30 / 90 / 365 days for ephemeral / standard / important.

AiProvenanceData.description: Where model-written text came from, so every client can say so.

sources.description: What the prompt carried, in order.

ArrivalData.description: One message that arrived, with the modes its conversation went to.

in_inbox.description: The message is in the provider's inbox.

modes.description:
The mode its sender's rule sent it to (the sender decision, list
headers, the address), with its one-word `tag`. Empty when it
arrived out of the inbox or from someone screened out.

is_update.description:
Derived: true when the daemon has seen a prior REQUEST with the same
UID and a lower SEQUENCE — i.e. this is a rescheduled / amended
invite.

viewer_attendee_email.description:
Derived: the email of the matched viewer attendee, as it appears in
the iCal `ATTENDEE` property. Used by the comment-compose path so the
REPLY's `ATTENDEE` matches exactly.

oneOf.description:
Derived: the PARTSTAT of the attendee whose address matches one of the
viewing account's addresses. `None` if no attendee matched or if
multiple matched ambiguously (the strict send path errors instead).

CalendarPartstat.description:
Typed view of an iCalendar `PARTSTAT` value, derived for the viewing
account's own attendee row. Maps 1:1 to the strings defined in RFC 5545.

ClientKind.description:
Originating client for an IPC request. Carried on the envelope so the
daemon's activity recorder can tag rows with the surface that produced
them. Legacy clients (pre-source-field) decode as `Cli` — the most
realistic guess for scripts hand-rolled against the socket.

ClosenessData.description:
How close you are, from your history with them: reciprocity, recency
and longevity (Whittaker, Jones and Terveen, CSCW 2002).

ComposerData.description: The box at the bottom, already addressed.

reply_all.description: Reply all is on by default in a group, off on a one-to-one topic.

asymmetry.description:
`|inbound - outbound| / max(inbound, outbound)` in `[0, 1]`. 0 means
perfectly balanced; 1 means I never responded (or vice versa).

ConversationData.description: The selected topic, as a conversation.

earlier_count.description: Earlier messages left out of a long thread.

ConversationMessageData.description: One message in a conversation, as its new text.

ask_quote.description: The ask, verbatim, when this message makes it: clients highlight it.

only_quoted.description:
Nothing but quoted text: `text` is the "(only quoted text)"
placeholder, and the message as sent is the way to read it.

text.description:
What this message says that the thread didn't already: quotes and
signature removed, the same text in every client.

trimmed_label.description:
"trimmed: quote, sig", when something was removed. `o` (or `v`)
shows the message as sent.

envelopes.description:
The newest arrivals, capped so one event always fits an IPC frame.
A large initial backfill carries a sample, not the whole batch.

total.description:
How many messages actually arrived. Equal to `envelopes.len()` for
an ordinary sync; larger when the batch was capped. Additive with a
serde default so an older client still decodes the event.

The default cuts the other way too: an event from a pre-0.6.25
daemon carries no `total` and so decodes as `0`, which is smaller
than the `envelopes` it shipped with. Readers must treat
`envelopes.len()` as the floor (`total.max(envelopes.len())`)
rather than reporting the zero.

oneOf.description:
A pending auto-reminder fired because its window elapsed without
a reply being detected. Carries the original outbound message
the user wanted to be nudged about.

Optimistic UI rollback hint: provider/store rejected some or all of a
tracked mutation (see `Request::Mutation.client_correlation_id`).

This client's event stream lagged and the daemon dropped
`skipped` broadcast events before it could deliver them (the
per-client channel filled during a burst, e.g. a large bulk
mutation or initial backfill). The client's cached views may now
be stale, so it should do a full resync. Sent point-to-point to
the affected client only — never broadcast.

A list-row gist queued by `Request::GetThreadGists { generate: true }`
is written (always `status: ready`).

A timed reply later came back: the message is in the reply queue
again and its conversation on the desk. Sent once per return, even
across restarts.

DeferKindData.description:
How a conversation is deferred, decided by who wrote last (the desk's
own rule).

DeferredThreadData.description: What deferring one conversation did, or with `dry_run` would do.

oneOf.description: Absent when the conversation was not found.

error.description: Why this conversation was not deferred. The others still are.

oneOf.description: Absent when the conversation could not be deferred (see `error`).

The message the time is set on: their latest message for reply
later, yours for waiting.

DeliveryData.description: A tracked delivery for the Deliveries surface (CLI/web/TUI).

message_ids.description: Source message ids (provenance). Populated by GetDelivery.

oneOf.description: Latest contributing thread, for "open in mailbox".

DeliveryItemData.description: One ordered/shipped item within a delivery.

created.description: Candidates the heuristic created (or would create on a dry run).

dry_run.description: Whether this was a preview (no writes).

shortlisted.description: Candidates handed to the LLM for confirmation.

updated.description: Candidates merged into an existing delivery.

DeskDoneItemData.description: One desk item to mark done: "nothing for me to do here, put it away".

commitment_id.description: A promise under Due: Done resolves it. Required for `due`.

oneOf.description:
The lane the row is in. Omitted: `waiting` when you wrote last,
otherwise `owed`, by the desk's own rule.

DeskDoneOutcomeData.description: What Done did to one item, or with `dry_run` would do.

oneOf.description: Absent when the conversation was not found.

archived.description: Messages taken out of the inbox (You owe and New from people only).

dismissed.description: Kept off the desk until someone writes in the conversation again.

error.description:
Why this item was not done. Other items still are; running Done
again retries it.

reminders_cancelled.description:
Pending "bring it back if no reply" reminders cancelled, so the
conversation doesn't come back on its own.

reply_later_cleared.description: Messages taken out of the reply-later queue.

resolved_commitment_id.description:
The promise resolved (Due only). Other open promises on the
conversation still show under Due.

DeskElsewhereData.description: Counts for everything that is not on the desk, for the one-line summary.

deliveries.description: Deliveries that have not arrived and were not dismissed.

invites.description: Upcoming invites you have not answered.

paper_trail.description:
Inbox mail from automated senders (receipts, notifications) in the
recent window.

reading.description:
Inbox mail from newsletters and lists in the recent window, read or
not: never an unread count.

screener.description: Senders with recent mail and no screener decision.

oneOf.description:
The first account (in account order) with senders waiting on a
screener decision, so a link from an all-accounts desk opens a queue
that has them.

DeskLaneData.description:
One lane: the rows returned (capped by the request's `lane_limit`) and
how many there are in total.

DeskLaneKind.description:
Which part of the desk a row belongs to. A thread appears in at most one
lane; when it qualifies for several, the earlier lane in this order wins.

until.description:
The instant the client previewed, as RFC3339. Never a phrase: resolve
it with `/api/v1/mail/time/resolve` and send the chosen `at`.

DeskRowData.description: One row on the desk: a thread, who it is with, and why it is here.

age_seconds.description:
Seconds from `since` to `generated_at`. Negative for a promise that
is not due yet.

back_at.description:
The row is back because a time you set came: reply later on You
owe, "bring it back if no reply" on Waiting on. The time you set.

commitment_id.description: Due rows: the promise's id, for resolving it.

message_id.description:
The message to open: the latest inbound message for owed and
people-new rows, your latest message for waiting rows, the promise's
evidence message for due rows.

message_ids.description:
Every message of the thread in this account, so a verb on the row
(archive, snooze) covers the whole conversation.

overdue.description: True when the row is past the person's usual pace, or past its due date.

reason.description: A short human reason, e.g. "replied to your message".

since.description:
When the clock for this row started: their message for owed and
people-new, your message for waiting, the due date for due.

starred.description: Any message in the conversation is starred.

usual_samples.description: How many past replies `usual_seconds` is based on.

usual_seconds.description:
The usual time for the relevant reply with this person: yours to them
on owed rows, theirs to you on waiting rows. Median of past replies.

DeskThreadRefData.description: A conversation, named with its account.

draft_path.description: The compose session file, as the other compose routes take it.

time_zone.description: The browser's IANA zone, so "by Friday" resolves where the user is.

oneOf.description:
`due_phrase` resolved by the natural-time parser in the caller's
zone. None when the phrase names no date the parser understands.

due_phrase.description:
When it is due, copied from the message ("by Friday"). Checked
against the text, so it is never the model's invention.

what.description: The deliverable as a short clause, such as "send the deck".

DoctorFinding.description:
One actionable issue identified by `mxr doctor`. Combines a short
human-readable message with optional shell commands the user can
run to remediate.

remediation.description:
Shell-runnable suggestions the user can copy-paste. Empty when
no automated remediation is available.

DoctorFindingCategory.description:
Coarse category of a doctor finding. Lets clients group related
issues without parsing free text.

DoctorFindingSeverity.description:
Severity of a doctor finding. Drives whether the CLI exits non-zero
(`Error`) and how the TUI styles the entry.

findings.description:
Structured findings: per-issue category, severity, and
shell-runnable remediation steps. Replaces the freeform
`recommended_next_steps` for clients that want to reason about
individual problems (TUI, future agent integrations). The
freeform field is preserved for backwards-compatibility.

allOf.description:
The body, as either a markdown source or a supplied HTML document.
Flattened so the JSON stays flat: `body_markdown`, or
`body_html`+`body_text`.

oneOf.description:
Per-message From override. `None` sends from the account's primary
address (default). `Some(addr)` sends from a specific owned address
(the primary or a registered alias); the daemon validates ownership at
send time and rejects a `from` the account does not own. The name falls
back to the account's display name when the override carries none.

inline_assets.description:
CID-referenced inline images for an HTML body. Always empty for a
markdown draft.

oneOf.description:
Set when this draft is the user-comment compose path for an iCal
invite REPLY. The outbound builder emits the special
`multipart/alternative` (text/plain + text/calendar;method=REPLY)
layout when this is `Some`. The daemon's send-completion hook reads
`source_message_id`+`partstat` to update the local store's PARTSTAT
after the email lands in Sent.

DraftContentSchema.description:
Documents the flattened [`DraftContent`] wire shape for OpenAPI.

`DraftContent` hand-rolls its serde impls to stay backward compatible, so
a derived schema on the enum itself would describe the Rust shape rather
than the JSON. This mirrors what actually goes over the wire.

body_html.description: Present on HTML drafts. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.

DraftEvalCaseData.description:
One replayed reply from `mxr draft eval`: the draft the model wrote from
what was known just before the user replied, next to what they sent.
Local only; never recorded in the activity log.

greeting_match.description: Both open the same way (or neither greets).

invented_numbers.description: Numbers in the draft that appear nowhere the model could see.

placeholders.description: `[[?: …]]` gaps the model left for the user.

sign_off_match.description: Both close the same way (or neither signs off).

invented_number_rate.description: Share of drafts with at least one invented number.

median_length_ratio.description: Median of draft words / actual words (1.0 is the user's length).

DraftProvenanceData.description:
Where an AI draft came from: the model that actually answered, whether
the user's other mail reached it, and the messages it read, so clients
can say so and open each source. Describes the request as it ran (the
provider pinned for it), not the configuration.

conversation.description:
Messages of the conversation being answered that fit in the prompt,
oldest first. Empty for a new message or a refine.

history_used.description:
Something from the user's other mail reached the model: their past
emails, the writing habits drawn from them, or the relationship
summary. False when the privacy gate kept it back (a cloud model
without `llm.allow_cloud_relationship_data`) or there was none.

model.description: The model that wrote the draft, as its endpoint named it.

oneOf.description:
The humanizer's second model pass (to read less machine-made): who
ran it and whether its text was used. Absent when no pass was due.

voice_examples.description:
The user's own past emails the model was shown to copy their voice,
in the order the prompt carried them.

DraftRewriteProvenanceData.description: The model pass that rewrites a draft after it was written.

history_used.description: The rewrite saw the user's habits and past emails, to keep the voice.

model.description: The model that answered the rewrite (or would have, when skipped).

rejected_by.description:
A later pass, after the text that was kept, whose answer was
dropped: this model saw the draft too.

proposed_send_at.description:
When set, the safety pipeline runs the send-time check
against the recipients and emits a `Severity::Info` issue
if the proposed slot is materially slower than the fastest
historic bucket. `None` = check skipped.

DraftSourceData.description: One message a draft was written from, in the user's own mailbox.

person.description: The other person's address: who the user wrote to, or who wrote it.

body_word_count.description:
Word count of the rendered body, snapshot at sync time. Used together
with `link_count` to classify newsletter-shaped mail into
`LinkDensity::Heavy`. `0` if the body word count wasn't computed
(older rows pre-backfill).

keywords.description:
Custom IMAP-style keywords (`$Forwarded`, `$NotJunk`, user-defined
`$Work`, etc.). System flags continue to live in `flags`. Stored
case-preserved as received; equality is case-sensitive to match
IMAP atom semantics.

label_provider_ids.description:
Provider-specific label IDs (e.g. "INBOX", "SENT", "Label_123").
Transient: used during sync to populate the message_labels junction table.

link_count.description:
Count of external links in the body after filtering out tracker /
unsubscribe / list-management hostnames. Drives the tri-state
"link" indicator on the mail list and the `has:link` search filter.
`0` means no link indicator.

desk's You owe lane: mail from people, in the inbox, from someone
you are in conversation with, ranked by how far past your usual
pace with them it is. `all` returns the raw list instead: every
thread whose latest inbound has not been followed by an outbound,
ranked by overdue ratio.

Fetch a single locally-stored draft by id (for editing in place).
Returns `ResponseData::Draft`; errors when no such draft exists.

Update a locally-stored draft in place, keyed by `draft.id`. Preserves
the draft's `created_at`; only drafts still in `'draft'` status are
editable. Errors when the draft is missing or already sending/sent.
Save draft to the mail server (e.g. Gmail Drafts folder).

List drafts that look orphaned mid-send: status `'sending'` with
a stale `last_heartbeat_at` (or `status_updated_at` fallback)
older than 1h. Surfaces what the daemon-startup recovery loop
would also auto-reset.

Force-reset an orphaned `'sending'` draft back to `'draft'` so
the user can retry the send. Idempotent: already-`'draft'` rows
return the no-op variant. `'sent'` rows refuse.

In-band authentication handshake for token-bearing transports
(phase 5, transport adapters). Raw framed IPC carries no headers, so a
transport with no implicit peer identity (`PeerAuth::TokenRequired`,
e.g. the TCP-loopback adapter) authenticates by sending this as the
FIRST request on the connection. The serve core gates every other
request on that connection behind a successful `Authenticate`, replying
`IpcErrorKind::Auth` until then. On transports that DO carry implicit
trust (UDS peer creds, in-process, stdio) the handshake is a harmless
no-op that returns [`ResponseData::Authenticated`]. Additive only — no
`IPC_PROTOCOL_VERSION` bump: old clients never emit it, and the only
transport that requires it (TCP) is itself new.

token.description:
Bearer token, matched against the daemon's token store (env
`MXR_DAEMON_TOKEN` or the daemon token file).

oneOf.description: Paginated reverse-chron list of activity rows.
Total matching rows (UI badge counts).
Grouped counts over a time window.

Export matching rows in CSV / JSON / NDJSON. When `path` is set the
daemon writes the file; otherwise it returns the body inline (capped).

Tombstone rows (set `redacted=1`, clear `context_json`). Either
`ids` is non-empty OR `filter` is `Some` — not both, not neither.
Hard-delete rows older than `before_ts`. Retention pruner uses this.
Stop recording new rows. `until_ts=None` is indefinite.
Resume recording.
List all saved filter presets, most-recently-used first.
Fetch a single preset by slug.
Create or update a preset (slug is the primary key).
Delete a preset by slug.

Resolve a time phrase ("fri 3", "tomorrow 9am", "in 2d") in the
daemon's local zone with the user's snooze hours. Read-only; clients
preview with it and send the chosen instant to the real mutation.

now.description:
Anchor for relative phrases. Defaults to the daemon's clock;
set it for reproducible output.

time_zone.description:
IANA zone to resolve in, such as "Europe/London". The web app
sends the browser's zone because the browser may not be on the
daemon's machine; omitted means the daemon's local zone.

oneOf.description:
What the store knows about a conversation (relationship with the
main counterparty, whether you owe a reply, open promises). No
model; read-only. Returns `ResponseData::ThreadContext`.

One-sentence gist and the ask, from the configured model, cached per
thread and latest message. Read-only. Returns
`ResponseData::ThreadGist`; an unavailable model is a status, not an
error.

The desk: what needs you rather than what arrived. Replies you owe,
promises coming due, threads waiting on someone, and new mail from
people, each row with a reason; plus counts for everything else.
Pure local store reads, no LLM. `account_id: None` covers every
enabled account.

lane_limit.description: Rows returned per lane; each lane still reports its full total.

oneOf.description:
"Done waiting": take threads you wrote last off the desk's Waiting
lane until a new message arrives in them. `dry_run` returns the same
selection without writing.
Undo `DismissDeskThreads`: the threads wait again.

Find promises the sender makes in a draft or a sent message, with
each due phrase resolved in `time_zone`. Read-only and capped by a
short budget, so a send never waits on it. Returns
`ResponseData::Promises`; an unavailable or slow model is a status.

now.description: Anchor for relative due phrases; defaults to the daemon's clock.

time_zone.description: IANA zone to resolve due phrases in; defaults to the daemon's.

oneOf.description:
Keep a promise from a message you sent as an open commitment due at
`due_at`, so it comes back when due. Idempotent per message and
promise: recording it again moves the date. `dry_run` returns what
would be stored without writing. Returns `ResponseData::RecordedPromise`.

The To do runway: Now, Coming up by week, Later, Whenever and Done
this week, with the headline, the empty state and the catch-up
count. `mark_seen` records that To do was opened, so the next
"expired since you last looked" counts from now. Returns
`ResponseData::TodoRunway`.

Rows in one state, newest change first: `expired` is the Expired
list. Returns `ResponseData::Todos`.

One row with every field's provenance. Takes a full id or a unique
prefix. Returns `ResponseData::Todo`.

Tick off, reopen or mark "not a to-do". Returns
`ResponseData::TodoChange`.

Show the row on your own date ("mon 9am", "in 3d", RFC3339), or
clear it with `when: None`. Resolved in `time_zone`, else the
daemon's. Returns `ResponseData::TodoChange`.

Correct fields; the row is yours from then on. Returns
`ResponseData::TodoChange`.

Make a to-do from a message yourself. `kind` defaults to `other`;
`due` is a phrase or RFC3339. Returns `ResponseData::TodoChange`.

The first run's one-time catch-up batch. Returns
`ResponseData::TodoCatchup`.

Keep or let go in the catch-up; `let_go_all` takes every row still
waiting. Returns `ResponseData::TodoChange`.

How a mode explains itself: header, empty states, first-encounter
card, why template and keys, with whether the card was retired.
`mode: None` returns every shipped mode. Returns
`ResponseData::ModeGuides`.

Retire a mode's first-encounter card on this profile, so it stays
closed in every client; `seen: false` brings it back. Returns
`ResponseData::ModeGuides` with the one mode.

Now, the front page: People, Due soon, one Updates card and an
evening Reading pick, at most three items each, with "and N more"
lines and the clear state. Local reads only. Returns
`ResponseData::Now`.

The rail: Now, the five modes and Inbox in order, each with its
key, count, badge (work only: Now) and whether it is built or an
early version on an existing view, plus the pages under More.
Returns `ResponseData::Rail`.

Which modes hold a thread and why, computed from the desk's lanes,
open to-dos, the sender classifier and per-mode done marks. Name
the thread by `thread_id`, by one of its messages, or many at once
in `thread_ids` (at most 100). Returns `ResponseData::ModeMembership`.

Done here: the thread leaves `mode` until a new message arrives
(To do ticks its open rows off). When no other mode holds the
thread and `modes.archive_on_last_done` is on, it is archived at
the provider too. Each outcome carries the handoff copy. `dry_run`
returns the same plan without changing anything; the real run
returns one `mutation_id` for `UndoMutation`. Archive has no done.
In To do, `todo_ids` ticks off only those rows; To do lets go of a
thread only once none of its to-dos is open. `sender` adds every
thread of that sender's in the mode (Updates or Reading), resolved
here so the preview and the run cover the same set. Returns
`ResponseData::ModeDone`.

Messages: people you talk with, one row each, in four bands (Your
turn, Pinned, Recent, Quiet), each row with its topics, a preview
of what they asked and your usual pace. Your turn shares the one
owed rule with Now. `turn` keeps only rows where it is that side's
turn; `limit` caps Recent and Quiet (totals count everything).
Local reads only. Returns `ResponseData::Messages`.

One person's page (or a group's): the relationship line, every
topic, and the selected topic as a conversation of new texts.
`person` is a row id (`person:<email>`, `group:<thread_id>`) or an
address. `topic` picks the conversation; by default the one whose
turn it is, else the latest. Returns `ResponseData::PersonPage`.

Got it: a short acknowledgement on `thread_id`, in your usual
greeting and sign-off for that person, built from a template with
no model. A preview (the default) returns the exact plan and a
`preview_token`. A send (`dry_run: false`) needs that token, issued
within the last minute, and the previewed text: it goes only when
the recipient, sender, target message and text all still match,
and never twice for the same message. Returns
`ResponseData::MessagesAck`.

Merge addresses into one person, by hand (D117): `into` becomes the
person's primary address. `dry_run` shows the result without
storing it. Returns `ResponseData::PersonMerge`.

Take an address back out of its person. Returns
`ResponseData::PersonMerge`.

Merges mxr suggests: the same name on addresses you've written to.
It never merges on its own. Returns `ResponseData::MergeSuggestions`.

Archive's ledger: records newest first by transaction date, one page
of `limit` from `offset`, with month counts and totals, facet counts
and the "coming up" strip over every matching record. Local reads
only. Returns `ResponseData::RecordLedger`.

One record's card: every field with its provenance, its documents
and its source emails. Takes a full id or a unique prefix. Returns
`ResponseData::Record`.

The answer box. A query that matches record fields returns the field
asked for, with no model; only when no record matches does it fall
back to `ArchiveAsk` (when `fallback`), and says so. Returns
`ResponseData::RecordAnswer`.

limit.description: Records in "also matching" after the answer.

oneOf.description:
Correct a record's field, confirm it, or confirm the whole card. A
correction is yours from then on and wins over every re-run.
`apply_to_sender` with an issuer name renames this sender's issuer
on every record, now and later. Returns `ResponseData::RecordChange`.

"Not a record" (or back again with `restore`). The email is never
touched, and a dismissed record is never filed again. Returns
`ResponseData::RecordChange`.

File an email as a record by hand, as `kind` when given. The dry run
returns the card that would be filed, from the same plan the real
filing writes. Returns `ResponseData::RecordChange`.

Always or never file mail from this message's sender (`verdict:
None` clears it). "Always" also files the sender's mail already
here. Returns `ResponseData::RecordChange`.

Export the matching records as CSV, and their PDFs to
`attachments_dir` when given. The dry run reports the row count,
totals, unchecked rows and missing PDFs for the same rows. Returns
`ResponseData::RecordExport`.

A place (Reading or Paper trail): inbox mail of that kind grouped by
sender, newest bundle first, each with the reason it is there.
`account_id: None` covers every enabled account.

message_offset.description:
Messages to skip in each bundle, for paging through one
sender's mail (pinned messages list first).

messages_per_bundle.description: Messages listed per bundle; counts always cover the whole bundle.

oneOf.description: Why one message is where it is: its kind, rule and reason.

Move a sender to a kind for this and all future mail, or with
`kind: None` return it to automatic. Stored as the sender's screener
decision (People: allow, Reading: feed, Paper trail: paper trail,
Screened out: deny).

Pin or unpin messages: a pinned message stays put when its bundle
or place is swept. Local to this machine.

Archive every unpinned message in a place, or in one sender's bundle.
`dry_run` returns what would be archived and a `preview_token`. The
real sweep needs that token and archives only what the preview
listed that is still in the place and still unpinned, never mail
that arrived or moved in since, as an undoable archive job.

preview_token.description: From the dry run; required when `dry_run` is false.

oneOf.description:
The desk's Done: nothing for me to do here, put it away. You owe and
New from people rows are archived, marked read and kept off the desk
until someone writes in the conversation again; Waiting on rows are
marked read and done waiting; a Due promise is resolved and its
conversation marked read. `dry_run` returns the same plan per item
without changing anything. The real run returns one `mutation_id`
for `UndoMutation`, which puts messages, dismissals and promises
back as they were. Returns `ResponseData::DeskItemsResolved`.

Gists for list rows, many conversations at once. Returns the cached
gists that still match each conversation at once, without calling a
model. With `generate`, conversations from people that have none are
queued for a background writer, in the order given (put the rows on
screen first); each gist arrives as `DaemonEvent::ThreadGistReady`.
A newer request goes ahead of older ones, and asking again for a
queued conversation never queues it twice. At most 100 ids. Returns
`ResponseData::ThreadGists`.

Reply later, or wait, until `until`, per conversation by who wrote
last: when they did, reply later (off the desk and out of the reply
queue until then, back in both at the time); when you did, bring it
back if nobody replies (off Waiting on until then; at the time,
unless someone replied, back on Waiting on and in the reply queue).
`until` is the instant the client previewed, never a phrase, and
must be in the future. `dry_run` returns the same plan without
changing anything. The real run returns one `mutation_id` for
`UndoMutation`, which puts the flags and reminders back as they
were. Returns `ResponseData::ThreadsDeferred`.

Request.description:
Every command a client can ask the daemon to perform.

Tagged `cmd` on the wire. One flat enum is the whole client-facing
surface: the CLI, TUI, web bridge, and MCP server all speak these same
requests, which is what keeps daemon capabilities client-agnostic (see
[`IpcCategory`] for the conceptual grouping). Mutations are expressed as
explicit commands with dry-run/preview options rather than free-form
state writes.

Response.description:
The daemon's reply to a [`Request`], correlated by [`IpcMessage::id`].

Either `Ok` wrapping a [`ResponseData`] payload, or `Error` with a
human-readable message plus a machine-readable [`IpcErrorKind`] so
clients can branch on failure class instead of parsing strings.

backfilled.description:
Calendar-invite rows rebuilt from body metadata that was already
parsed but missing a `calendar_invites` row.

rehydrated.description:
Messages re-hydrated from the provider because they carried a
calendar attachment but no parsed calendar metadata (e.g. Gmail
invites whose `.ics` arrived only as an attachment). Defaults to 0
for older daemons.

oneOf.description: Returned by `Request::GetFreshness`.
A single locally-stored draft, returned by `Request::GetDraft`.
List of messages currently flagged for reply-later.
Returned by `Request::ListScheduledSends`.

Per-saved-search unread counts. Map shape so callers can do
fast id-keyed lookups when rendering the tab strip; missing
entries render as a bare label (no `(0)` clutter).
The model that rewrote the text, when one did.

Tone/length the daemon inferred from the relationship (the
effective values used, even when the caller overrode them) so
the UI can show "Matched to {sender}" without re-deriving.

What the draft was written from, for the "which model, whose
history, which emails" line.

Effective From address resolved (and ownership-validated) by
`Request::ResolveSendFrom`.

degraded.description:
The DB-backed part of this snapshot (`accounts`, `total_messages`,
`sync_statuses`) timed out and carries no reading: those three
fields are empty/zero because the daemon could not answer in time,
not because the store is empty or idle. Poll again rather than
concluding anything from them. The DB-free fields (versions,
`daemon_pid`, `feature_health`) are always a real reading.

oneOf.description:
Success reply to [`Request::Authenticate`]: the connection is now
trusted for the remainder of its lifetime (phase 5 token transports).

Returned by `Request::SendDraft` and `Request::SendStoredDraft` on

Returned by `Request::ExtractDraftCommitments`.
Returned by `Request::ListOwedReplies`.

Returned by `Request::GetDesk`.

Returned by `Request::SetSenderKind`. `previous` is the kind the user

Returned by `Request::PinMessages`: how many messages changed.

ResponseTimeBucket.description:
A single bucket of the response-time histogram. `count` rows had a
clock latency in `(prev_upper, upper_bound_seconds]`. The last
bucket uses `u32::MAX` as `upper_bound_seconds` to mean "no upper
limit".

ResponseTimeSummary.description:
Aggregate response-time summary for `mxr response-time`. p50/p90 in
seconds; business-hours percentiles are `None` until the reconciler has
backfilled the relevant rows.

histogram.description:
Distribution of clock latencies (seconds) bucketed for the
histogram view in the TUI / future CLI surface. Ordered from
shortest to longest by `upper_bound_seconds`. `#[serde(default)]`
so older daemons returning the previous payload deserialize
cleanly during a rolling upgrade.

Role.description:
Well-known role for a `Label`/folder, mirroring MSP §2.3. The set
covers the roles every consumer-mail provider exposes; provider-specific
roles outside this set are represented as `None` so clients fall back
to generic styling. New variants land additively under
`#[non_exhaustive]` to keep wire compatibility cheap.

SavedActivityFilterEntry.description: Wire shape of a saved activity filter preset (Phase 8).

ScheduledSendData.description: One draft waiting to be sent later.

last_attempt_at.description:
When this draft last fired, if it fired before and was then
rescheduled (for example after a failed or blocked send).

last_attempt_outcome.description:
Outcome of that firing: `sent`, `blocked`, `failed` or
`interrupted`. The error text itself is not persisted.

ScreenerQuestionData.description:
A first-time sender's one question, asked on their row in the mode
their mail landed in (D117). Answering is `SetSenderKind`.

choices.description: The answers, the current mode's first.

newest.description: Newest message timestamp in this group (Unix seconds).

oldest.description: Oldest message timestamp in this group (Unix seconds).

proposed_at.description:
Slot the caller asked us to evaluate, echoed back so JSON
consumers don't have to rebuild it. Present only when the
caller passed `proposed_at` on the request.

oneOf.description: `null` or omitted: back to automatic.

SenderKindData.description: What kind of sender mail comes from, and so where it lives.

StaleThreadRow.description:
Single row of `mxr stale` output: a thread whose latest message points
at one party and has been silent past the threshold.

StorageBucket.description:
Single row of `mxr storage` output: how many bytes / how many items
rolled up under a particular grouping key (sender, mimetype, label).

archived_unread_count.description:
Messages that landed in ARCHIVE without ever being read. Strong
"this is noise" signal for the unsubscribe ranker.

opened_count.description:
Number of messages from this sender that have been marked READ.
Combined with `message_count` gives the open-rate used by `unsub --rank`.

replied_count.description:
Stable JSON field. The subscriptions query currently returns zero;
reply-pair counts power sender/contact analytics, not this ranker.

preview_token.description:
From the dry run's preview; required unless `dry_run`. The sweep
archives only what that preview listed.

SweepPreviewData.description:
What a sweep archives. The dry run and the real sweep build this from
the same selection; the real sweep only ever narrows the preview's.

count.description: Messages that will be (or were) archived.

pinned_excluded.description: Pinned messages left where they are.

preview_token.description:
Hands the previewed selection to the real sweep, which archives
only those messages. Expires after a few minutes and works once.
Absent when nothing would be archived.

sample_subjects.description: Up to five subjects, newest first.

SweepSenderData.description: One sender a sweep would archive mail from.

SyncErrorData.description: The last sync failure of one account.

message.description: The provider's own words, for the details view.

retry_at.description: When the daemon will try again, when it has scheduled a retry.

SyncErrorKindData.description: What kind of failure stopped the last sync.

SyncHealthData.description:
How an account's sync is doing, least worrying first: the "All
accounts" scope shows the last one in this order.

SyncProgressData.description:
How far the sync pass running for an account has got.

`current` counts messages committed so far in this backfill run, carrying
across provider pages. `total` is the denominator when the provider can
say how much is left — the fake provider knows its dataset exactly, Gmail
and IMAP cannot count what remains without paying for it, so it stays
absent for them.

message_ids.description:
Constituent message IDs ordered by `date` ascending, ties
broken by `MessageId` ascending. Empty `message_ids` denotes
a tombstoned thread (typically the loser side of a
mail-threading merge); clients receiving such a Thread in
`SyncBatch.threads_changed` SHOULD drop any cached metadata
for that id.

oneOf.description:
The sentence that makes the ask, verified by the daemon to appear in
that message's text (whitespace-insensitive), so clients can
highlight it. Dropped when it can't be found.

summary.description: The ask in a short plain-text clause, at most 160 characters.

ThreadContextData.description:
Returned by `Request::GetThreadContext`. Computed from the local store
with no model involved.

oneOf.description:
The person this conversation is mainly with: the latest sender who
isn't you, or the first recipient of your latest message.

Set when the newest message is from someone else, it isn't bulk
mail, and you haven't written in the thread since.

promises.description: Open promises recorded against this thread, both directions.

bulk_sender.description: Mailing-list or bulk sender; relationship stats mean little here.

last_contact_elsewhere_at.description:
Latest message between you in any other thread. `None` means this is
your first conversation.

messages_from_them.description: Messages they sent you, across every thread.

messages_from_you.description: Messages you sent them (to, cc or bcc), across every thread.

their_reply_p50_seconds.description: Median time they take to answer you.

your_reply_p50_seconds.description: Median time you take to answer them, from past reply pairs.

ThreadGistBatchData.description:
Returned by `Request::GetThreadGists`: the gists a list can show now,
straight from the cache, and what was queued to be written.

gists.description:
Cached gists that match each conversation's newest message, in
request order. Only `ready` gists are listed.

in_flight.description:
Conversations a writer is on right now; their gists arrive as events
too.

model.description:
Whether gists can be written at all. Anything but `available` means
lists show their rows as they are, with nothing to wait for.

queued.description:
Conversations waiting in the queue after this request. Each one's
gist arrives as a `ThreadGistReady` event.

skipped.description: Conversations that have no gist and won't get one from this request.

oneOf.description:
What the conversation asks of you. `None` with `status: ready` means
the model found no ask.

gist.description: One plain-text sentence, at most 240 characters.

oneOf.description:
The conversation's newest message when the gist was written. A client
that has seen a newer message in the conversation ignores the gist.

reason.description: Why there is no gist, for `disabled`, `blocked` and `failed`.

generate.description:
Queue missing gists for people's conversations; each arrives as a
`ThreadGistReady` event.

thread_ids.description: At most 100, in the order to write missing gists (visible rows first).

ThreadModesData.description: Every mode one thread is in, returned by `Request::GetModeMembership`.

done_in.description:
Modes this thread was marked done in and stays out of until a new
message arrives.

held_by.description:
The modes keeping it in the provider's inbox: Inbox's "held by To
do" chip. Archive never holds.

in_inbox.description: Any message of the thread is in the provider's inbox.

modes.description: In rail order. Empty when no mode holds it (Inbox still shows it).

ThreadPromiseData.description: An open promise in the thread and who made it.

owner.description:
Who owes it, as the thread knows them: "you" for your own promises,
else the owner's display name from the thread's messages, falling back
to their address. In a group thread each promise keeps its own owner.

ThreadShapeData.description: A thread's shape, judged in the daemon.

at.description:
The instant to store. Send this back to the mutation unchanged so
what was previewed is what is saved.

date_label.description: "Friday 3 October", with the year only when it isn't this year.

label.description: Short text for a choice chip, such as "15:00".

local.description: The same instant as RFC3339 in the resolving zone.

note.description: Set when a clock change moved or doubled the requested wall time.

TimeResolution.description: A phrase resolved to at least one instant.

choices.description:
Every reading, default first. More than one means the phrase was
ambiguous.

spans.description: Byte ranges of `input` that were understood.

TimeResolveError.description: Why a phrase didn't resolve, phrased for the user.

message.description: A calm, specific message with an example that works.

token.description: The word that wasn't understood, for `unrecognized` and `conflict`.

understood.description: Byte ranges understood before the problem.

TimeSpan.description: A byte range of the input the parser understood.

domain.description: The link's registrable domain, shown beside the label.

label.description: "Open email to pay", "Open email to verify".

oneOf.description: The email to open.

trusted.description:
Always false: nothing on a to-do is trusted to open directly. Kept
so earlier clients read the action as untrusted.

url.description:
The link in that email the action is about, to highlight there.
Not an action: never open it from the row.

TodoActionKindData.description: What the row's primary action does.

already_over.description: What the first run found already over, by kind.

already_over_line.description: "Already over, so not shown: 50 past invites, 63 quiet parcels."

overflow_count.description: Found for the batch after it was full; in the Expired list.

title.description: "Catch up: 12 things from the last two weeks might still need you."

oneOf.description: Every row still waiting in the batch.
Back to undecided in the batch: the undo of keep or let go.

TodoCatchupDecisionData.description: Keep or let go in the catch-up.

TodoChangeData.description:
Returned by every to-do mutation. With `dry_run`, `changed` is what
would change and nothing was written.

action.description: done | undo | dismiss | schedule | edit | create | keep | let_go

changed.description: The rows as they are (or would be) after the change.

summary.description: One line saying what happened: "Ticked off 2.", "Would let go of 12."

unchanged.description: Ids that matched but were not in a state this change applies to.

title.description: What to do, starting with the verb.

TodoData.description: One row: a thing to do, titled verb plus object, never the subject.

act_by_at.description: When you must act: due minus processing time.

due_words.description: The phrase the due date was read from, verbatim.

kind.description:
bill | payment_failed | renewal | document | lease | return | rsvp |
verify | sign | promise | other

next.description:
What happens next, where it's true: "When the receipt arrives, the
row says it looks done."

origin.description: rule | schema | ics | model | handoff | manual

runway.description: How far the runway bar is filled, from surfacing (0) to due (1).

surface_at.description: When the row shows up in Now.

user_touched.description: You made or changed it: it never expires and re-runs leave it be.

when_label.description:
"act by Wed 7 Oct · due Fri 9 Oct", "was due Fri 9 Oct", "shows up
Mon 12 Oct", "no date".

edits.description:
title, due, amount, counterparty or kind; an empty value clears due,
amount and counterparty.

TodoEditData.description:
One edit: `field` is title, due, amount, counterparty or kind; an
empty value clears due, amount and counterparty.

checked.description:
False for a guess to confirm, such as a numeric date that reads
differently in UK and US order. Shown with an open dot.

evidence.description: The words it was read from, or how it was worked out.

field.description:
title, kind, counterparty, amount, due_at, act_by_at, surface_at,
relevant_until, action_url, event_start

source.description: schema | ics | rule | table | model | user

source_label.description: "a pattern in the email", "the lead-time table", "you".

TodoFirstRunData.description: How far the newest-first first run has got.

TodoKindCountData.description: A kind and how many, for "Already over, so not shown: 50 past invites".

TodoNextData.description: The next row to show up, for the empty state.

TodoRunwayData.description: Returned by `Request::GetTodoRunway`: the bands, ready to draw.

catchup_count.description: Rows waiting in the one-time catch-up.

coming_up.description: Showing up in the next 30 days, by week.

empty_state.description: Set when Now is empty: what lands here, or when the next thing does.

expired_since_last_looked.description: "3 expired since you last looked", when above zero.

headline.description:
"3 things need you this week. Council tax first, act by Wed." Empty
when Now is.

now.description: Shown now, by act-by; overdue rows after the ones still in time.

time_zone.description: The browser's IANA zone, so "mon 9am" means the user's Monday.

when.description: "mon 9am", "in 3d" or RFC3339; omitted clears your date.

dry_run.description: Preview only: the rows that would change, nothing written.

week_start.description: The Monday the week starts, in the user's zone.

TopicStateData.description: Whose turn it is on one topic.

TrimmedData.description: What `new text` removed from a message.

footer.description: A legal disclaimer or a tracking/unsubscribe footer.

list_share_of_inbound_pct.description: 0.0–100.0; share of inbound messages that came via a list_id.

oneOf.description: Single fastest reply pair in the window.

Single slowest reply pair in the window. Capped at 30 days to
exclude the pathological "I replied 8 years later" cases.

WrappedSummary.description:
Year-in-review summary returned by `mxr wrapped`. Combines volume,
time-pattern, contact, reply-discipline, storage, newsletter, and
superlative sections so the CLI can render a single narrative panel.

busiest_date.description: The single calendar day with the most activity, and its count.

busiest_day_of_week.description: Day name and message count for the busiest day-of-week (Mon–Sun).

busiest_hour_utc.description: Hour 0–23 (UTC) and message count for the busiest hour-of-day.

day_of_week_distribution.description:
Per-day-of-week message counts. Index 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday.
`#[serde(default)]` keeps older daemons compatible.

hour_distribution.description:
Per-hour message counts (UTC), indexed 0..=23. Powers the
hour-of-day chart in the TUI Wrapped view.
`#[serde(default)]` keeps older daemons compatible.

most_emailed_by_me.description: Top 5 recipients I emailed by outbound count.

most_emailed_to_me.description: Top 5 senders to me by inbound count.

bearer.description: Token from the `bridge-token` file in the active profile's config directory, or from `[bridge].token_path` / `MXR_BRIDGE_TOKEN_PATH` when either is set. Send via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Browser WebSocket clients can use the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: bearer, <token>` subprotocol. The `?token=<token>` query string is accepted only by `/api/v1/events` for command-line WebSocket fallback.
